decisions.title: Sandbox on by default
decisions.context: Agents run inside a sandbox: an operating-system fence that lets their commands touch only the project folder and a short allow-list of package sites. It stops a tricked agent from sending files elsewhere; the cost is an occasional blocked download that needs a one-line allow-list entry.

options.label: Keep it on
options.detail: Safer; a few installs need the allowlist.

decisions.why: Blocks exfiltration paths at no cost for normal work.

decisions.title: --force-with-lease on feature branches
decisions.context: When an agent updates its own PR branch after a rebase (replaying its commits on top of the newest main), git refuses a normal push. Force-with-lease means "overwrite my branch only if nobody else pushed to it since I last looked", so it cannot erase someone else's work. Plain --force and any push to main stay blocked either way.
decisions.why: Agents keep their PR branches current without ever being able to overwrite work they have not seen.
